titre: American Psycho Reboot Is 'Not Happening,' Director Says
chapo: We won't be getting a version of American Psycho from the director of Challengers
extrait: We won't be getting a new take from the director of Challengers A couple of years ago, reports emerged that Challengers and Call Me By Your Name director Luca Guadagnino was working on his own reimagining of American Psycho, the 2000 film adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' novel. Unfortunately (or fortunately, depending on your point of view), it doesn't appear his new take on the cult-hit psychological thriller will see the light of day. Luca Guadagnino was first linked to a new American Psycho adaptation written by Contagion's Scott Z. Burns in October 2024. We had not heard much more about the project since then, so Deadline asked Guadagnino about it during the director's recent appearance on its Crew Call podcast. Sadly, Guadagnino did not have a positive update on the project. “Scott Z. Burns wrote a fantastic script. Unfortunately for me, as we speak, it’s not happening," Guadagnino succinctly explained. American Psycho is a horror novel originally released in 1991, but it's mostly remembered for Mary Harron's 2000 film adaptation starring Christian Bale. The movie, which explores themes of toxic masculinity and materialism, was a subversive horror comedy for its time. Despite its very grim subject matter, Bale's over-the-top performance and key scenes from the movie have nestled their way into pop culture and become memes in the 26 years since the original's release. Even official accounts for kid-friendly franchises like Pokémon have referenced it. Any new adaptation will have lofty expectations to live up to and will likely have to face the reality that many of the things the book lampoons have only gotten worse in the decades since its original release. Sadly, it looks like we'll never quite know how Guadagnino and Burns planned to reinterpret American Psycho for the modern day. This new rendition of American Psycho isn't the only Luca Guadagnino project that hasn't come to fruition in recent years. He was attached to direct a movie based on Sgt. Rock for DC Studios, but that project was shelved before it could start shooting in 2025. Artificial, a movie about the founders of OpenAI, will be the next Guadagnino film to hit theaters. It'll be released on Dec. 25.

titre: American Psycho Remake From Director Luca Guadagnino No Longer Happening
chapo: Director Luca Guadagnino has confirmed his American Psycho remake is officially dead.
extrait: Director Luca Guadagnino has confirmed his American Psycho remake is officially dead. The Challengers and Call Me by Your Name movie maker delivered the disappointing news when asked for an update on Deadline's Crew Call podcast. He admitted the script for the project that he read, which was penned by the writer behind The Bourne Ultimatum and Side Effects, was "fantastic" but not something he can continue working on. "American Psycho, which is a fantastic script from Scott Z. Burns, unfortunately, is not happening for me, as we speak," Guadagnino said. Guadagnino has more than proven himself as a name capable of handling the weight of a property on the level of American Psycho, which is exactly why movie fans were so excited to hear he could be attached to the project in 2024. Although fans have referred to what would have become his slice into the well-established movie universe as a 'remake,' at the time of its announcement, Lionsgate teased that the project would have been more of an adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' American Psycho novel, rather than a remake of Christian Bale's 2000 movie. Updates on Guadagnino's American Psycho have been few and far between in the years since its announcement, though. Elvis star Austin Butler was once in the running for the role of Patrick Bateman, as was Euphoria's Jacob Elordi. It was reported in October 2025 that the film would not gender-swap its lead role. Bale eventually went on to comment on Guadagnino's reimagining and another actor bringing his iconic character to the big screen. He said "all the best to 'em" just earlier this year, adding, "I like brave people." The director didn't explain why his version of American Psycho won't be moving forward, just that it's "not happening for me." While that means any version of American Psycho won't be coming to movies anytime soon, it's unclear if Lionsgate has completely closed the door on Patrick Bateman. With Burns' script finished, there's always the chance a different filmmaker could take the reins. For now, though, it's best to assume the American Psycho remake/adaptation is well and truly dead. In the meantime, Guadagnino is gearing up for the release of his Sam Altman biopic, Artificial. The film is gearing up for a limited premiere Christmas 2026 before getting a wider release January 8, 2027. Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN.
